newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish one-day same-share deals need new rules - KPW.
newsitem.headline: Polish one-day same-share deals need new rules - KPW.

text.p: Trade in same shares at a single Warsaw bourse session could take place if the bourse allows for it in its official rules, the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) said in a statement on Tuesday.

The KPW said it made its statement after press reports that several brokerage houses had allowed a confirmation of trade execution to represent purchases of shares at the bourse's regular single-price-auction session that were sold later in the day in continuous trade.

Such transactions were made physically possible after the bourse's introduction of longer sessions from January 2, in which continuous trade follows the regular single-price-auction session rather than the two running simultaneously.
The KPW said the bourse would have to recognise the trade confirmation certificate as a legally binding document to allow same-share, single-session trade.
"That would require attendant changes in the (bourse's) binding rules and the introduction of additional regulations defining that document (the information on executed orders)," the statement said.
The bourse officially settles all transactions three days after trade.
The KPW said that since no such rules were currently in place it would penalise any brokerages it found guilty of overstepping the regulations.
